tn.quote: The data for this variety comes from Swanton & Mendoza Ruíz (forthcoming). … The tone system of this variety is not further elaborated on, but the correspondences are very systematic. Tones are marked with numbers in this source (C3). This variety has three level tones (low, mid, high) and one contour tone (falling). The high tone does not appear on the first mora and the contour only appears in the second mora combining with a mid tone. This results in 7 contrastive tone melodies. The glottal stop does not affect tones.
tn.cite: Auderset, Sandra. 2024. Rates of change and phylogenetic signal in Mixtec tone. Language Dynamics and Change 14(1): 1-41. doi:10.1163/22105832-bja10031. Supplementary Material 'Standardization of tone notations' (15 Aug 2022, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.10143870).

tn.note: Three level tones (low, mid, high) and one falling contour, assigned per mora; high never on the first mora, the fall only on the second mora with mid, giving 7 contrastive two-mora tone melodies.

tn.quote: iv.) Sinyar has a system of two contrastive level tones (Low/High, more briefly L/H). tn.note: Two contrastive level tones, Low and High, plus frequent lexical downsteps at the beginning, middle or end of a word (a final downstep lowers a following low-toned clitic); nothing on word stress.

tn.quote: Nous avons identifié trois tons ponctuels phonémiques en ngbugu: haut [á], moyen [ā] et bas [à]. Les tons modulés, en ngbugu, sont des combinaisons de tons ponctuels, par ex.: [vōtàá] trois (ton montant), [mīndúù] cinq (ton descendant). Il existe aussi des tons ponctuels longs qu’on analyse comme une séquence de tons ponctuels, par ex.: [zòò] longtemps. … Nous avons constaté des oppositions tonales entre des mots, par ex. [kú] punaise, [kū] cuisse, [kù] plaie (v. tableau ci-dessous). Comme il y a plusieurs paires minimales tonales, on écrit tous les tons.
tn.translation: We have identified three phonemic level tones in Ngbugu: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]. Contour tones in Ngbugu are combinations of level tones, e.g. [vōtàá] 'three' (rising tone), [mīndúù] 'five' (falling tone). There are also long level tones, which we analyse as a sequence of level tones, e.g. [zòò] 'a long time'. … We have found tonal oppositions between words, e.g. [kú] 'bedbug', [kū] 'thigh', [kù] 'wound' (see table below). Since there are several tonal minimal pairs, all tones are written.
tn.cite: Adoumacho, Jessé-Joël, Tychique Longbo, Guy-Florent Matchi & Kenneth S. Olson. 2020. Précis d'orthographe du ngbugu [Orthography Statement for Ngbugu]. Bangui: ACATBA et SIL International. 26 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 86801; issued 2020-03).
tn.locator: §3 'Les tons' and §3.1, p. 8
tn.note: Three level tones, high, mid and low, with a minimal triplet kú 'bedbug', kū 'thigh', kù 'wound'; rising and falling contours are level-tone sequences; verb tone marks aspect, negation, future.

tn.quote: This paper has examined the results of instrumental analysis on the tones of the Tai Ya language as spoken in Yunnan, China. The Gedney box wordlist was utilized as the basis for analysis. tn.quote: Like most Nigerian languages, Tarok is tonal. There are three level tones and two contour or gliding tones. The tones are marked as follows: High (H) ´ Mid (M) marked by the absence of a tone mark Low (L) ` Falling (HF) ̂ Rising (LR) .̌ … The level tones have a very wide distribution, but the gliding ones are not only rare, but they occur mainly in grammatical contexts and in some syllable deletions. The rising tone is indeed very rare. Both kinetic tones are glides from high to mid and low to mid for the falling and rising tones respectively.
tn.cite: Longtau, Selbut R. 2008 [2022 edited electronic edition]. The Tarok Language: Its Basic Principles and Grammar Sketch. Jos: Development Alternatives, Research & Training (DART). xiv+241 pp.

5594.idn: Name in the source: latege (la langue latege); family in the source: groupe de langues tékés, Bantu B.71 (classification de Guthrie 1971)

tn.quote: 3 Les tons En latege il existe deux niveaux de ton: haut et bas. Il n’est pas nécessaire d’indiquer le ton sur chaque mot, puisque pour la plupart des cas il n’y a pas d’ambiguïté. Dans la grammaire, certaines paires de conjugaisons de verbes se distinquent uniquement par la tonalité des affixes. Dans l’orthographe, on les distinguent par des caractères spéciaux écrits devant le verbe dans une de chaque paire de conjugaisons: * distingue le futur du présent: … % distingue le progressif passé de l’habituel passé :
tn.translation: 3 Tones. In Latege there are two tone levels: high and low. It is not necessary to mark the tone on every word, since in most cases there is no ambiguity. In the grammar, certain pairs of verb conjugations are distinguished solely by the tone of the affixes. In the orthography they are distinguished by special characters written before the verb in one member of each pair of conjugations: * distinguishes the future from the present: ... % distinguishes the past progressive from the past habitual:
tn.cite: Linton, Pauline. 2016. L'orthographe du latege. Édition préliminaire. Léconi (République Gabonaise): Global Outreach Mission. 15 pp.
tn.locator: sec. 3 'Les tons', p. 7
tn.note: Two tone levels, high and low; certain pairs of verb conjugations differ only in the tone of their affixes. Orthography sketch: tone-bearing unit, downstep and word stress are not discussed.

tn.translation: (3) Tones. 1. High level, written ˥ (55); e.g. bγ˥ 'carry on the back'. 2. Mid level, written ˧ (33); e.g. bγ˧ 'insect'. 3. Low level, written ˩ (11); e.g. bγ˩ 'drift'. 4. Short tone, written ˨ (2); e.g. bγ˨ 'Bodhisattva'. Note: the short tone (2) is a very short tone; after it the syllable closes in a glottal stop [ʔ]; since the glottal stop is an appendage of this tone we do not write it. When citation tones are read together with other words there is often tone sandhi: the negatives ma˩ 'not' and t'a˩ 'don't', if followed by a high-level (55) verb, lower it to mid level (33) … and to express a hypothetical mood the verb of the clause is often changed to a low rising tone …

5603.idn: Name in the source: dialonké (dialonké de Faléya); family in the source: langue mandé-nord, apparentée de très près au soso (Creissels 1989, Keita 1989); Mande, Western branch, Susu-Jalonke group 'группа сусу-дьялонке' (Vydrin 2017); the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: Le dialonké a un système tonal réductible à deux unités tonologiques de base, |H| et |B|, et les tons lexicaux du dialonké coïncident presque toujours avec ceux du soso, dont le dialonké est dans l'ensemble très proche. Mais le dialonké se distingue du soso par la complexité de ses règles de réalisation tonale. … on constate en effet que les syllabes CV ne peuvent être associés qu'à un unique ton simple (H ou B), tandis que les syllabes CV: aussi bien que CVC peuvent être associées à une séquence tonale HB ou BH. Par exemple: kwɛ́ɛ̀ "nuit", sún ̀ "jeûne",tàá "village", sàn ́ "jambe"
tn.translation: Dialonké has a tonal system reducible to two basic tonological units, |H| and |L|, and the lexical tones of Dialonké almost always coincide with those of Soso, to which Dialonké is on the whole very close. But Dialonké differs from Soso in the complexity of its tone-realisation rules. … one observes that CV syllables can only be associated with a single simple tone (H or L), whereas CV: as well as CVC syllables can be associated with a tonal sequence HL or LH. For example: kwɛ́ɛ̀ 'night', sún ̀ 'fast', tàá 'village', sàn ́ 'leg'
tn.cite: Creissels, Denis. 1989. Structures syllabiques du dialonké de Faléya. Mandenkan 18: 1-30.
tn.locator: sect. 7 'Règles tonales et structures syllabiques', pp. 20-21
tn.note: Two level tones, high and low (Faléya dialect, Mali); words carry set schemes (H, HL, LH, LHL); a floating low downsteps a following high. The Fouta Djallon variety described by Lüpke has lost tone.

5613.idn: Name in the source: mbuun (B87); Mbuun (Mbunda); parlers d'Imbongo; parler d'Idiofa

tn.quote: La langue mbuun a recours à deux tons simples H et B. Les réalisations contextuelles de ces deux tons en modulation conduisent à des tons montants et descendants. Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. Le ton descendant est plus fréquent que le ton montant. Toutefois, malgré le défaut de paires minimales opposant le ton descendant au ton montant, nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant).
tn.translation: The Mbuun language uses two simple tones, H and L. The contextual realisations of these two tones in modulation lead to rising and falling tones. These modulated tones result from contacts between two simple tones. The falling tone is more frequent than the rising tone. However, despite the lack of minimal pairs opposing the falling tone to the rising tone, we think that Mbuun has four tonal registers: H, L and HL (falling) and LH (rising).

corr.words: Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. ... nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant). ... Néanmoins, dans la mesure où il existe des noms avec ce ton montant, même s'ils sont rarissimes ou ne s'opposent à rien d'autre, nous considérons ce registre.
